decisions.reason: After two years on the market, the maintenance oil line appears to fit the core floor-care system well and is inexpensive to continue, so management would keep it while using the added learning to support selective refinement rather than withdrawal.
The moisture-protection underlay strengthens the firm's system offering and likely carries limited continuation cost, so with no clear negative signal management would keep it in the portfolio.

The high-density underlay foam remains worth keeping as a complementary option, but because it is more standardized and potentially overlaps with other underlays it still has the highest rationalization risk among the surviving products.

The oak parquet line is close to the firm's core capabilities and strategic positioning, and after another year of market exposure management would usually keep it while concentrating resources on the better-performing variants rather than exiting the line entirely.
